intended_object: The pullback φ^* : Div(E₂) → Div(E₁) of divisors along an isogeny φ : E₁ → E₂ (Silverman II.3): for a place P' of F(E₁), the coefficient of φ^*D at P' is the ramification index e(P'|P) times the coefficient of D at the place P = φ(P') below it. Equivalently, it is Stichtenoth's conorm for the extension F(E₁)/φ^*F(E₂). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body applies the library's general conorm, `TauCeti.Divisor.conorm`, to the extension F(W₂) → F(W₁). That extension is given by the algebra structure, and the hypothesis `h` requires its structure map to equal `φ.fieldPullback`, the F-algebra map that pulls functions back along φ. Two auxiliary facts derived from `h` supply the instances the conorm needs: the scalar tower F ⊆ F(W₂) ⊆ F(W₁), and the finiteness of the extension (which gives integrality and finite fibres).

The conorm sets the coefficient at P' to e(P'|P)·D(P), where P is the restriction of P' to F(W₂). That is exactly the textbook formula φ^*(Q) = Σ_{P∈φ⁻¹(Q)} e_φ(P)·P, extended additively. Places of the function field correspond to the points of the projective curve, including the point at infinity, so no point is left out. The direction is also right: the map is contravariant, Div(W₂) → Div(W₁), for φ : W₁ → W₂.

This is a thin wrapper around the general construction, specialised to isogenies. The general notion (the conorm for any algebraic extension of function fields with finite fibres) already exists in the library in full generality, and Mathlib has no divisor-pullback notion that this re-implements. Pullback along an isogeny is a standard, specific object, so the definition is not too narrow.
